The most important part is finding out the direct link to the picture you want to post. If you use Firefox, right-clicking on an image and choosing "copy image location" will copy the correct link to your clipboard.

If you use chrome, right clicking on an image and choosing "copy image URL" will do the same as above.

Honestly, I'd say I'm an expert in none. I'm a complete amateur with absolutely zero art history background (I didn't even really get interested in art until a few years after college, in my early 30s now), and probably most people with an interest in art could analyze me under the table while I attempt to keep up with a glazed over look in my eyes.

As far as personal interest, I guess I'd say I'm more partial to realism but I definitely appreciate aspects of all styles. What I generally find most appealing is a certain level of "darkness" (don't really know how else to describe it, which I'm sure shows my total ignorance as far as art analysis). I really enjoy artists who are able to take a certain amount of "darkness" and turn it into something beautiful, which is what I like about Van Gogh, and even Edward Hopper. I know it wasn't Hoppers intention, but I love the sort of voyeuristic loneliness in his paintings.

I think a good way to describe that might be a use of light and shade, or using a predominantly dark value scale. There is a style called chiaroscuro that you might like. It may be too heavy on the darks for your taste but, eh might as well give it a look see.
